quests.title: The Strip Outside Lapstone
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. A metre of dirt between the fence and the footpath at Lapstone, dead for 10 years and not dead now. I have rung the number on the letter four times. Council mows on the fifteenth and does not know what is in it. Stand near it and stop the man with the whipper snipper. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

steps.label: the strip, which is a garden now
the man with the whipper snipper
photograph it while it still exists

quests.title: Night Fill, Waitara
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. Ten to six, nobody in the building but us and a radio that gets one station. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. Somebody has been taking things and they know our roster, which means they come in off the late train at Waitara. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.

steps.label: come in on the late one like they do
the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning

quests.title: The Window Above Bardwell Park
quests.blurb: I am told you do odd jobs. 12 years above Bardwell Park. It started small, the way these things do. I do not hear the trains any more, which means I hear it instantly when one of them is wrong. Since a Tuesday the joins sound different. You'll know it when you see it.

quests.title: The Clock at Rosehill Gardens
quests.blurb: This is going to sound small. The clock on the Rosehill Gardens platform has been four minutes fast since I got here and every relief who comes through wants to fix it. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Do not fix it. Find out who set it that way, before they retire. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

to Tramway Avenue, where the old crew drink

quests.title: The Dog at Asquith
quests.blurb: Right. Since you asked. A dog meets the 5:40 at Asquith every weekday and nobody gets off for it. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Four months of this. I have decided it is not going to be a sad story. Find out whose it is. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: the end of the platform, at twenty to six

the street it walks home to

quests.title: The Book at Granville
quests.blurb: Do not laugh. I run a small book on things that are not races — weather, delays, whether the the second express out of Granville runs on time. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Somebody is beating it by information, not luck. Ride the run they ride. There's cash in it. Not a lot.

quests.title: Last Service out of Pymble
quests.blurb: It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. The last one through Pymble carries four people and one of them is always asleep. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Ride it to Gordon, photograph the platform with nobody on it, and come back and tell me the place still exists when there is no one in it. You'll know it when you see it.

steps.label: ride the late one to Gordon
the empty platform, lit and pointless
tell them what you saw

quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. A card ending 18 boards at Dulwich Grove on a Tuesday and vanishes. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. Not a fare thing — ninety cents. I want to know *how*, and they keep sending a different bloke. Do that and we're square.

the gap in the fence everyone knows about
photograph it before somebody welds it
